target_customer: Patients with bleeding disorders, hemophilia treatment centers and biopharma sponsors that pay for real world evidence
problem: Rare disease patients lack tools to track treatment and bleeds, and drug makers lack real world outcome data collected at the point of care.
business_model: Free patient app and provider dashboards, monetized through pharma sponsored real world evidence and research programs

founders.name: Miguel Lara
prior_employers: Global bank (healthcare managing director for 10+ years, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page claims 15+ years as a digital health startup CEO.

founders.name: Marc Lara
founders.background_notes: YC page cites experience launching products for new therapeutic areas and clinical and HEOR studies.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile tracking app with provider dashboards; later compliance work (HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 13485) added overhead but not research grade technology.

defensibility.rationale: Company claims over 33 percent of U.S. prophylaxis hemophilia patients and over 50 percent of treatment centers, which are self reported, and a pharma sponsor base that is hard to rebuild.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pfizer publishes a competing HemMobile app (date of launch not established). Microhealth stayed independent and lists Novo Nordisk, Sanofi, Roche and Pfizer as sponsors.

market_need_then: A 2015 TechCrunch profile described the company as trying to crowdsource management of rare chronic conditions starting with hemophilia, where patients had few digital tools.

branding.domain_note: YC lists microhealth.com; app stores point to microhealth.org.

identity.voice_and_tone: Patient friendly and compliance heavy ('We build products people love', 'You own your data').

rebrands.why: Not stated; app store listings show both names

brand_strength.rationale: Known within the hemophilia community per company figures, but no press or community evidence about the brand itself and the name is generic.

pivots.from: Consumer app for chronic illness management
pivots.to: Rare disease real world evidence platform for biopharma
pivots.why: Not documented with dates; the YC page now describes a care delivery and evidence generation platform

outcome_analysis: Microhealth began as a chronic illness app launched in 2015 and narrowed to hemophilia and other rare blood disorders. It reports retention of 52 months and pharma sponsors, and it is still active with about 25 staff. No institutional funding was found, so growth appears to be a slow, sponsor funded niche business.
notes: Founded year follows the YC page (2015); a TechCrunch summary says the brothers started it in 2011. Funding: CB Insights shows about 120K with YC and a Plug and Play entry dated 2022, while Getlatka says bootstrapped with no outside funding; none verified, so no rounds recorded. No dated competitor source near August 2015 was found (only current Similarweb lists). All traction figures are self reported on the YC page and company site.
